packets.responsibility: Converts vtracer's raw cubic-bezier/polygon contour output into Paper.js Segments, then a 3-phase recognition pipeline over each traced shape: Phase 1 fits a complete ellipse (RMSE-gated) or rounded-rect (area-ratio plus an exact closed-form corner-radius recovery) so common flat graphics land as REAL editable paramShapes (corner-radius handles, Motion cornerTL..BL/arcStart/arcSweep) instead of frozen bezier blobs; Phase 2, for a shape Phase 1 could not fit whole, looks for a neighboring traced shape sharing a straight cut seam (vtracer's 'cutout' hierarchical mode guarantees non-overlapping regions, so paint order is irrelevant), strips points on that seam, and retries an algebraic least-squares circle fit (Kasa method) with an angular-coverage gate specifically to reject the osculating-circle false-positive a long smooth curve can otherwise trigger. buildShapeItem assembles one Path (single contour) or CompoundPath (multi-contour, e.g. a donut) per traced shape, built detached (insert:false) and reparented via addChildren rather than relying on Paper's constructor-option auto-insert, which the file's own comment says was confirmed unreliable for a 2-contour donut case.

A naming collision exists between SMRigWidget (this census's on-canvas joystick/slider layer type, CLAUDE.md §13) and app.js's entirely separate, undocumented 'Bone Rig' feature (ld.rig = {bones,ikChains,binds}, skeletal deformation binding either a Path by strokeId or an image-mesh Raster by meshId). Both are called 'rig', both are unrelated in purpose, and the bone-rig feature's direct consumption of image-mesh.js's data model (SMImageMesh.get(meshId)) is undocumented anywhere in CLAUDE.md §12/§13.

Every new on-canvas gesture owner that needs to win a pointerdown race against motion.js's (or another bridge's) own capture-phase listener on #canvas-area has independently re-derived the same fix: register on `document` at capture phase instead, since a listener on an ANCESTOR always fires before one on the target element regardless of registration order among siblings. rig-widget.js, image-mesh-bridge.js, and tracker-panel.js all carry this fix with near-identical comments; viewtools-bridge.js's shouldRotate() Alt-drag exclusion list shows the same problem solved the opposite (accreting, hand-maintained) way - grown one tool name at a time, each added only after a live bug report that a specific tool's own Alt+drag gesture was being stolen. A future tool adding a new on-canvas gesture is likely to hit one of these two problems on day one unless a shared mechanism is introduced. Separately, rig-bridge.js (Rig tool: Tracer/Assigner/Deplacer) does NOT have this fix - its listeners sit on #canvas-area, not document - and this census found a plausible, but unconfirmed, path by which a Rig-posing click during Motion mode could be silently stolen by select-bridge.js's unconditional Motion-mode hit-test; flagged as an open question for live verification, not a proven defect (see C04b.deform.rig-tool's own notes).

window.showContextMenu (ui.js, 14 consumer files including 3 in this census) and the document-level scrub-input mechanism (ui.js, CLAUDE.md §10, 16 consumer files) are the two highest-fan-in contracts in this whole census - one a function-call API, the other a bare CSS-class DOM contract. Either one's signature/behavior changing has unusually broad blast radius across both this census and its siblings.

window.effectParamValueAt (effects-panel.js, nominally 'editor chrome') is directly read by engine-bridge.js's live per-frame render path (sceneEffectsOf) to resolve keyed effect-parameter values, with only a silent same-shape fallback if the global is absent. Part of this docked-panel file's surface is therefore load-bearing rendering/evaluation logic, not purely UI - an extraction boundary between 'editor presentation' and 'rendering' must preserve engine-bridge.js's load-order dependency on this specific global rather than treating the whole file as movable UI chrome.

Boolean-op hygiene is good across this entire census: every CompoundPath-producing operation reachable from the 49 files here (eraser-bridge.js's pixel/vector erase, fill-bridge.js's fillMergeSameColor, group-bridge.js's flattenGroup, draw-bridge.js's fill-brush self-union) was traced and confirmed to route through tools.js's insertBooleanResult (sibling census C04a) rather than inserting a raw multi-source boolean result directly - no violation found anywhere in this batch.

Test coverage is extremely uneven across this census: text-selector.js (tests/text-selector.test.cjs, 18 pure-Node cases) and image-mesh.js (tests/fixtures/mesh + fixtures.test.cjs's 'mesh'/'mesh-vertex-world'/'mesh-propagated' checks) each have genuine, dedicated, checked-in oracles. vector-text-bridge.js has a real fixture (tests/fixtures/text) plus opt-in Playwright coverage. The remaining ~44 files - all tool bridges (draw/eraser/fill/pen/shape/gradient/group/audio/perspective/reference/rulers/viewtools/rig/vectorize/feedback), all of ui.js, all brush/preset pickers, and most standalone panels - have zero automated behavioral coverage; several (e.g. draw-bridge.js, stroke-modeler.js) have only a source-text regex shape-check, not a behavioral test.

CLAUDE.md drift confirmed in several places, all independently verified against current source rather than assumed: feedback-bridge.js's actual browser-preview localStorage key differs from §6's documented key (see DEF-7); image-mesh-bridge.js's native-video-layer mesh support (feedback #779, 2026-09) and its maskImageWithShape() freehand-outline substitute both postdate and are not mentioned by §12/§12bis (dated 2026-08-30); and §12ter's PR3 vertex-keyframe machinery (meshVertexOffsetAt, meshVertexRowCount) is described as part of image-mesh.js but is actually owned entirely by motion.js (outside this census) - image-mesh.js only supplies the poseAt() callback contract that machinery calls into.

state.audioTracks (audio-bridge.js) is explicitly, by design, outside the undo snapshot (layersSnapshotNow) - every mute/volume/offset/trim/split/rename/delete on an audio track is therefore not undoable via the normal undo stack, visible after the fact only via SMFeedback's action log. This is a documented tradeoff in the file's own header, not an oversight, but it is a real behavioral gap relative to every other edit surface in the app and is not surfaced to the user anywhere in the UI.

Several UI-facing popovers independently reimplement the same small 'wavy-stroke demo preview' helper (sample a sine wave, trace dabs/segments along it) with no shared code: brush-preset-picker.js, brush-editor.js, and bitmap-tip-picker.js each carry their own copy. Low correctness risk (none is a source of truth for anything) but a real, low-cost consolidation opportunity alongside the toLocalPoint (DEF-11) and easing-curve (DEF-12) duplications.

CLAUDE.md §1's explicit consumer list for 'construction of selectedPaths' (select-bridge.js, tools.js, timeline.js) is stale: shapes-panel.js's applySelection also directly push/splices window.selectedPaths in its additive Shift/Alt-click branch, a real fourth writer not documented there. Not a bug - the feature is deliberately built and tested - but worth folding into that list so a future family-of-bug-#1 audit does not miss it.

known_defects.summary: onDown/onUp write `erasing = false;` to an undeclared, unread implicit global (also at line 259) - dead code with no functional effect, but a real silent global leak with no 'use strict' in effect.

Neither brush-editor.js's Save action nor brush-preset-picker.js's custom-preset delete (×) button ever calls pushUndo() - state.customBrushPresets is real, exportJSON-persisted project data, so creating or deleting a custom vector-brush preset is silently un-undoable.

The 2026-09 divergence fix claims uncapped ddt 'stays pinned near 1/rate for any dt, however large', but the substep count is still clamped to Math.min(20000, Math.ceil(dt*rate)); once dt exceeds ~166.7s at rate=120 the cap saturates and ddt grows unboundedly again, reintroducing the same explicit-Euler divergence class the fix closed (moved from a ~0.42s threshold to ~167s).

openPanel() unconditionally calls pushUndo() once; only the Cancel button calls undo() to revert it. closePanel() has zero external callers (repo-wide grep confirmed), and the panel auto-hides via CSS on deselection - so opening the panel and deselecting without Cancel/Done strands one empty pushUndo() snapshot on the undo stack permanently.

onDown() calls pushUndo() unconditionally as soon as hitTest() finds any hit, before it is known whether the drag will move anything; onUp only gates updateUI() on drag.moved, not the snapshot. onDblClick() has the same shape - a zero-jitter click or double-click-to-reset can leave 1-2 empty undo snapshots.

triangulate() silently swallows any Delaunator exception and returns [] with no console.warn or user-facing diagnostic - a mesh that fails to triangulate (e.g. a pathological hand-drawn outline) silently renders as 'no mesh'.

CLAUDE.md §6 documents the browser-preview (no-Tauri) local storage key as localStorage['sm-feedback-<projectKey>'], but lsKey() actually uses 'nemo-feedback-' + projectKey() - a real prefix mismatch a support process following the documented key literally would miss.

window.SMFeedback.resolveFeedback and .deleteFeedback are exported but have zero call sites anywhere in src/ - only approveFeedback is wired to a real UI button (Feedback inbox's Approuver). Matches CLAUDE.md's own phrasing for resolveFeedback, which reads as a documented-but-manual/console API rather than a wired UI flow.

deleteCategory has no confirmation step and is irreversible - localStorage-backed and entirely outside the app's undo stack - so one click on a category tab's 'Supprimer l'onglet' context-menu item permanently deletes every preset filed under it with zero recovery path.

registerAllCustomEffects swallows per-effect shader-registration failures for both built-in and custom shaders via try/catch + console.warn only (lines 27-30, 33-36) - a saved custom shader that passes the naive /return\s+vec4/ regex validator but fails to actually compile degrades silently, e.g. after a project reload.

The Motion-transform world-to-local point mapper (toLocalPoint, feedback #135) is reimplemented near-identically 4 times - draw-bridge.js, eraser-bridge.js, pen-bridge.js, shape-bridge.js - each file's own comment cross-referencing the others by name rather than sharing one helper.

The on-curve-waypoint easing spline math (evalPointsCurve/tangentAt/segCtrl) is a fourth, hand-synced, currently-untested copy of the same math already extracted once into src/js/animation/curve.js (the 'R08 easing kernel', tested against camera.js/text-selector.js/animation/curve.js by tests/easing-reference.test.cjs) - ui.js's own copy is not in that test's enumeration. Both files' comments acknowledge the split, so this is known/accepted duplication, not a hidden defect - but it is CLAUDE.md §3's dual-implementation hazard class in JS rather than Rust.

bbox-containment hole/exterior classification for boolean-op-shaped results is now independently implemented in at least three places: svg-import.js's explodeLeaf (C05), tools.js's insertBooleanResult (sibling census C04a), and this file's contoursToMergedPaths - worth a single shared helper in any real extraction rather than a fourth reimplementation.
